value.title: Claim scan: literal kinds and metadata errors

sections.name: body
sections.value:
# Claim folder review: exact kind pairs and metadata errors

PR #342 at df1a9d9ef6da21d019b8588b381417b0d5a97604 exposed two allocation hazards:

- A generic kind whose literal name ends in `s` already has seeds `<kind>` and `<kind>s`. Stripping the suffix of both seeds admits a third, unrelated name: `status` unexpectedly scans `statu`. A literal-kind / plural pair must remain the authority.
- `Path::is_dir()` hides metadata errors. A parent with mode 0400 can be enumerated while metadata of its children fails; silently skipping them hands out an existing number. A scan refusal test must cover failed child metadata, not only `read_dir` of an unreadable seed folder.

Both isolated HTTP regression assertions failed at this head and passed with main's allocation scan. Decorated and nested decoys, non-ASCII lookalikes, files, other folder-scanning kinds and shallow symlink reads had positive controls. Auto-release for uppercase delivered paths is a separate bookkeeping problem: an open claim still prevents reuse. It remains a C35 proposal, not an excuse to widen this approved fix.

**Magic wand:** retain a shared claim-folder contract fixture covering both directory enumeration and delivered-path recognition, including generic kinds ending in `s` and real metadata errors. This prevents the help, allocation reader and release reader from drifting.

**Difficulties:** the dependency-free review tree's harness boot is NOT-READY, and quick checks fail on missing TS tools and ambient Biome skew. C25 remains authoritative: no dependency symlink or install; exact-head CI carries TS proof. Mutants were run from an owned git archive with the canonical shared target, nice19, one build at a time; only that owned directory was cleaned.

Current C34 is one reviewer, one round: author fixes; prime checks fix commits. Do not follow the older two-round memory entries.
